name: Barry Myers

summary.text: Barry Lee Myers, of Pennsylvania, was chief executive of the private forecaster AccuWeather and the younger brother of its founder Joel Myers. President Trump nominated him in October 2017 to be Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere, the post that heads NOAA. The Senate Commerce Committee held a hearing in November 2017 and reported the nomination three times on party-line votes, but the full Senate never voted; Democrats questioned his AccuWeather ties as a conflict of interest and his lack of a science degree. Myers resigned from AccuWeather and sold his interest in 2019, and the nomination was withdrawn in late 2019, with Myers citing cancer treatment.

facts.claim: The Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee held a hearing on Barry Lee Myers's nomination to be Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere on November 29, 2017 (S. Hrg. 115-647), and the Congressional Record of December 13, 2017 lists the nomination as reported by the committee.

sources.publisher: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation (congress.gov)
sources.title: Senate Hearing 115-647: Nomination hearing

facts.claim: The committee took up the nomination again at an executive session on January 18, 2018 after Myers was renominated, and in 2019 the committee approved the renominated nomination on a 14-12 party-line vote without holding a new hearing.

Myers Nomination for NOAA Administrator Clears Committee

facts.claim: The Senate's Daily Digest for December 2, 2019 records that the Senate received notification of the withdrawal of Myers's nomination; the full Senate never voted on it although the committee had sent it to the floor three times.

sources.title: Trump's embattled nominee withdraws, cites health woes

facts.claim: In withdrawing, Myers said in a statement that he had undergone surgery for cancer and received chemotherapy; the withdrawal came in a letter to the White House first reported by the Washington Times.

facts.claim: Myers resigned from AccuWeather in 2019 and sold his interest in the company in an attempt to satisfy Democratic senators who said his link to the company was a conflict of interest.
facts.quote: Myers resigned from AccuWeather earlier this year and sold his interest in an attempt to satisfy Democrats who said his link to the weather forecasting company constituted a conflict of interest

sources.title: Trump's embattled nominee withdraws, cites health woes

facts.claim: During the nomination it was disclosed that AccuWeather had paid $290,000 as part of a federal settlement of sexual harassment claims; Myers was never personally accused of harassment in connection with the case.
facts.quote: Myers was never personally accused of any harassment in connection with the case

sources.title: Trump's embattled nominee withdraws, cites health woes

facts.claim: CNN reported in October 2017, when Myers was nominated, that AccuWeather had lobbied Congress, NOAA and the Commerce Department on 'federal data policies' and had spent $40,000 in 2005 lobbying on commercial weather industry issues.

connections.claim: Myers was chief executive of AccuWeather at the time of his nomination to lead NOAA; he resigned and sold his interest in the company in 2019.

sources.title: Trump's embattled nominee withdraws, cites health woes

connections.claim: Myers was nominated to be Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere and NOAA administrator in the 115th and 116th Congresses; the nomination was withdrawn in December 2019 without a floor vote.
President Trump nominated Myers to head NOAA in 2017 and renominated him in January 2019.

sources.title: Myers Nomination for NOAA Administrator Clears Committee

openQuestions: Site claim 'AccuWeather CEO nominated to run NOAA ... The full Senate never voted, and he withdrew in 2019, citing health reasons' is supported.

Site description of AccuWeather as 'a private forecaster that benefits from limits on free public forecasts' is a characterisation; the sources opened document AccuWeather's lobbying on federal data policy but do not quantify any benefit.
The congress.gov PN numbers for the 2017, 2018 and 2019 nominations were not found; the owner may wish to add them from the congress.gov nominations database.
Sources differ on whether the 2019 renomination was sent to the Senate on January 16 or January 21, 2019.
